name: Steroid back acne management

card.summary: Back acne that people link to steroid use; reference material is limited to general acne and androgen information.
card.note: Severe acne is usually managed by clinicians; no dedicated trials found.

quick.overview:
Steroid back acne is acne on the back attributed to anabolic steroids or testosterone. It is a recurring topic in forum protocol discussions.

Thin sourcing is available here, so the article is short.
quick.mechanism: Androgens increase sebum production, which is linked to acne.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids carry broader legal and health risks; standard acne treatments are listed by general references.

lead: Steroid back acne, often shortened to bacne in training forums, is acne on the back, shoulders and chest that people connect with anabolic-androgenic steroid or testosterone use. For people building a physique, the skin of the upper body matters as much as the muscle under it, so managing breakouts there is a recurring topic in lifting and looksmaxxing communities [1][9].

Dermatology literature uses the term steroid acne for acne caused by corticosteroids or anabolic-androgenic steroids, and a 1989 review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology described a sequence of follicular changes leading to microcomedones and then inflamed papules and pustules [2][3]. Wikipedia lists testosterone and glucocorticoids among medications that can worsen acne, and calls the form caused by anabolic-androgenic steroids steroid acne [1].

Communities discuss the topic as a skin-clarity question: what causes it, how it differs from other back conditions, and when to see a dermatologist. No published trial has tested treatments specifically for back acne in anabolic steroid users; clinicians draw on general acne care [1].

chain: Androgens raise oil production in follicles
Clogged follicles become inflamed on the back and shoulders
Clearing or managing breakouts gives a cleaner-looking upper body
angle.text: People concerned about a visible physique treat back and shoulder breakouts as part of how their upper body looks. Discussion centres on recognising steroid-related acne, telling it apart from similar conditions, and conventional dermatology care.

infobox: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, antibiotics, isotretinoin (clinician-directed) [1]

paras: Androgens such as testosterone, DHT and DHEA are linked to acne because they increase sebum production, and acne does not develop in people with complete androgen insensitivity syndrome [1]. Acne favours skin with many oil glands, including the face, upper chest and back [1]. Wikipedia lists medications that can worsen existing acne, including lithium, glucocorticoids and testosterone, and uses steroid acne for the form caused by anabolic-androgenic steroids [1].

sections.h: Steroid acne in the medical literature
paras: A 1989 review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology said steroid acne had become more common with organ transplantation and cancer treatment regimens, and described a sequence of infundibular spongiosis, hyperkeratosis, microcomedo formation and rupture leading to papules and papulopustules [2]. A 2003 dermatology nursing article and a 2025 British Journal of Dermatology report on steroid acne fluorescing under ultraviolet light also address the condition [4][5]. Reviews of topical clobetasol list steroid acne among the effects of prolonged use of superpotent topical glucocorticoids [6].
A 1999 Japanese review found Malassezia in follicular contents of both steroid acne and acne vulgaris, which dermatologists note when distinguishing acne-like eruptions from fungal folliculitis [7].

Wikipedia lists first-line treatments for acne vulgaris as topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide and topical or oral antibiotics, with isotretinoin reserved by clinicians for severe cases, and notes azelaic acid and salicylic acid as other topical options [1]. Diagnosis includes a medication review, since drugs can contribute [1]. Forum participants on T Nation commonly recommend a visit to a dermatologist when breakouts are severe, and describe androgen-driven oil production as the cause [8].

No studies found examining management of back acne specifically in anabolic steroid users. Related literature covers steroid acne in clinical case descriptions and reviews [2][4][5], and a 1983 randomized trial found that topical betamethasone valerate on the face caused no significant change in skin flora compared with placebo [10].

timeline.event: Review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology describes steroid acne and its follicular sequence [2].
Dermatology Nursing publishes an article on steroid acne [4].

lore.intro: On T Nation, bacne appears in threads on steroid use, cruising doses and appearance, with members disagreeing about what it indicates and how to handle it [8][9][11].

claims.claim: Back acne means someone is on steroids
claims.believers: Some forum members treat bacne as a visible sign of anabolic steroid use in other lifters [12].
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes acne is largely genetic and also driven by androgens in general, and appears on the back in many people who use no steroids [1]. One T Nation member wrote that bacne does not automatically mean steroid use [9].

claims.claim: Excess androgens drive oily skin and breakouts during steroid use
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says acne during steroid use comes from sebaceous glands making more oil under high androgen levels, and suggests keeping skin clean and seeing a dermatologist if severe [8].
claims.experts: Dermatology sources link androgens to increased sebum production and acne, and describe steroid acne as a recognised medication-related form [1][2].

claims.claim: Estrogen conversion contributes to acne and sore nipples
claims.believers: A T Nation member recalled severe teenage acne alongside itchy nipples when testosterone and aromatase activity were high and asked whether the two were connected [11].
claims.experts: Reference sources list androgens and other hormones in acne; no published study cited here tests an estrogen-conversion mechanism for back acne.
